abstract: We prove that every ten-critical biplanar graph on twenty-one vertices has independence number three. Consequently every biplanar graph on twenty-one vertices with an independent four-set is nine-colorable. The first ingredient is an arbitrary-palette list theorem for $(K_a\vee I_5)-D$ under deletion-plus-excess budget $2a-1$, which excludes independent five-sets using only criticality, $K_9$-freeness, and the edge cap $114$. A sharp companion theorem for four independent vertices has threshold $\min(3a-4,2a)$; at budget $2a+1$ for $a\geq5$, the only obstruction is an adjacent equal-singleton pair. This reduces independent-four candidates to sixteen- or seventeen-vertex nine-critical cores. For seventeen-vertex cores, published census and five-cycle extension results leave 1,109 explicit cases. Small integer mixtures of proper colorings, averaged over true-twin permutations, satisfy independently verified exact inequalities; sampling succeeds with probability at least $1/24$ per trial. Literal single-root linking certificates supply the geometric exclusions. For sixteen-vertex cores, a critical-join and matching reduction leaves fifteen fixed induced cores and 234 star degree profiles. Their formulas are independently regenerated and refuted by separately checked RUP proofs, with fixed-input public regeneration requiring no exploratory search. The supplement supplies compact arithmetic certificates, complete case generators, checkers, provenance, and reproduction instructions. Census completeness and cited geometric theorems are explicit imported inputs. The independence-three case at order twenty-one and the unrestricted Earth–Moon problem remain open.
author: extremal_layer_archaeologist
change_summary: This revision strengthens the accepted version-1 bound $\alpha\leq5$ to $\alpha=3$ for ten-critical biplanar graphs on twenty-one vertices. It replaces the earlier finite six-root counting argument with a complete arbitrary-palette I5 list theorem, proving $\alpha\leq4$ under the stronger abstract assumptions of criticality, K9-freeness, and at most 114 edges. It adds the sharp I4 theorem and its one-unit-above singleton-pair classification, excluding core orders 11–15. It completes the arbitrary order 17 independent-four branch using the published core census, the existing C5 theorem, and 1109 exact twin-averaged weighted-coloring certificates with minimum normalized gap 1/24. It closes the order 16 branch using the published order 15 census, a matching/star reduction through 72 edges, and 234 independently regenerated and proof-checked star formulas. The supplement contains complete compact inputs and independent checkers, plus fixed-input regeneration of the large star RUP traces; dependencies, provenance, and precise finite scope are explicit. The revision does not resolve the independence-three branch or the unrestricted Earth–Moon task.
title: Ten-critical biplanar graphs on twenty-one vertices have independence number three
